questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Concepts of Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: Globalisation is the process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries driven by flows of goods, services, capital, technology and ideas; it has political, economic and cultural dimensions, and its intensification from the 1990s followed technological and policy changes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Concepts of Globalisation'.
questions.a: Globalisation compresses space and time: markets, media and movements knit distant places into instant interdependence.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Concepts of Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Concept of Globalisation (source: leps107.txt globalisation concept and dimensions sections)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Causes: Technology and Politics' refers to.
questions.a: Globalisation's causes are technological - container transport, telecommunications and computers collapsing costs - and political - liberalisation policies, WTO rules and the opening of economies like India's 1991 reforms that lowered trade barriers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Causes: Technology and Politics'.
questions.a: Both engines matter: cheaper movement of data and goods met deliberate decisions to open markets.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Causes: Technology and Politics' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Causes of Globalisation (source: leps107.txt technology, liberalisation and India's 1991 opening sections)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Consequences: Winners and Critics' refers to.
questions.a: Globalisation's consequences are uneven: consumers gain cheaper goods and workers gain new service jobs, while critics point to job losses in protected sectors, cultural homogenisation, and the widening gap between winners and losers within and between countries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Consequences: Winners and Critics'.
questions.a: The ledger splits by sector and skill: software exporters celebrate while import-competing farmers and workers bear adjustment costs.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Consequences: Winners and Critics' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Consequences of Globalisation (source: leps107.txt economic, cultural and political consequences sections)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India and Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: India integrated into the global economy after the 1991 reforms through trade, investment and services exports; globalisation brought growth, consumer choice and technology, alongside concerns for farmers, small industry and cultural practices, making India both a beneficiary and a negotiator of global rules.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India and Globalisation'.
questions.a: India's globalisation is selective: services globalised fast while agriculture and labour markets stayed partly protected.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India and Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: India and Globalisation (source: leps107.txt India's reforms, gains and concerns sections)
